title: Fix motion vectors lost when instances update between draws
body: 🤖 Fix motion vectors lost when instances update between draws > [!INFO] *AI disclosure*: This contribution was authored by an autonomous AI agent (Claude Code), on behalf of a user, to fix #119879. Fixes #119879. ### Cause Forward+ and Mobile keep each instance's previous transform for motion vectors. `set_transform()` records it on the instance's first move of a frame, identified by `RSG::rasterizer->get_frame_number()`. `_fill_render_list()` treats a move from an earlier frame as old: it sets `prev_transform = transform`, and the instance is drawn without motion. The frame number is incremented in `begin_frame()`, at the start of a draw, so between two draws it still holds the frame already drawn. Pending transforms are normally applied in `RendererSceneCull::update()`, after `begin_frame()`, and get the right frame. These apply them immediately instead: - `RendererSceneCull::free()` for an instance; - `instances_cull_aabb()`, `instances_cull_ray()`, `instances_cull_convex()`; - `instance_geometry_get_shader_parameter_list()`, used by `get_property_list()` on a GeometryInstance3D. When one of them runs after the frame's transforms reached the RenderingServer and before the next draw, the moves are marked with the old frame and the next draw drops their motion. An object that moves with the camera is then reprojected by the camera's motion and drawn doubled for that frame. `queue_free()` always lands there. `SceneTree::process()` calls `flush_transform_notifications()` and then `_flush_delete_queue()`, and `~VisualInstance3D()` frees the instance. The same calls made inside `_process()` come before the transforms are pushed, so they do no harm. ### Change - Add `RendererCompositor::get_frame_number_for_changes()`: the current frame between `begin_frame()` and `end_frame()`, otherwise the next one. It is implemented in the RD, GLES3 and dummy compositors. - Forward+ and Mobile `set_transform()` mark moves with it, so a move applied between two draws belongs to the next frame. - An instance's first transform starts its history. `instance_set_base()` sets it between draws, and it has no previous transform. `get_frame_number()` is left as it is: about 35 other places use it. Fixing how moves are marked covers every caller that applies transforms early, instead of changing each caller. ### Testing Test project: `engine-test-119879.zip` [engine-test-119879.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33494968/engine-test-119879.zip). The camera turns 1° a frame. One checkerboard panel is a child of the camera; another sweeps through the world. Every 30 frames a trigger runs. `run_matrix.sh` compares each of the 400 frames (MD5) with the same run without a trigger. | Trigger, every 30 frames | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `queue_free()` | 341 of 400 frames differ | 0 | | `RenderingServer.free_rid()` in `frame_pre_draw` | 341 | 0 | | `get_property_list()` in `frame_pre_draw` | 341 | 0 | | `RenderingServer.instances_cull_aabb()` in `frame_pre_draw` | 341 | 0 | | `RenderingServer.free_rid()` in `frame_post_draw` (nothing pending) | 0 | 0 | - The results are the same for FSR2 and TAA, with and without a teleport on the trigger frames, on 4.7.2-stable and `master`. - Without triggers, the frames are identical before and after the fix. - `--test` passes. Camera panel with FSR2, 5x zoom: the frame before, the frame with the queue_free(), the frame after, and the pixels that changed (orange: brighter, blue: darker).
